clues.q: These large Japanese drums are often performed in thunderous ensembles at festivals and concerts.
This Japanese idol group, named for Tokyo’s Akihabara district, released the hit “Heavy Rotation” in 2010.
Formed through the 2015 survival show “Sixteen,” this JYP Entertainment girl group includes Nayeon, Jihyo and Tzuyu.
This three-stringed Japanese lute, plucked with a large plectrum, accompanies kabuki and bunraku puppet theater.
Ancestor of the Japanese koto, this Chinese plucked zither usually has 21 strings and movable bridges.
Founded in 1985, this Japanese animation studio made “Kiki’s Delivery Service” and “Howl’s Moving Castle.”
In this 2021 Marvel film, Simu Liu plays a martial artist and Tony Leung plays his father, Wenwu.
clues.a: What is Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings?

clues.q: This Hong Kong action star, famous for performing his own stunts, teamed with Chris Tucker in 1998’s “Rush Hour.”
Starring Bae Yong-joon, this 2002 KBS romance drama became a huge hit in Japan and helped spark the Korean Wave there.
Hirokazu Kore-eda’s 2018 film about a makeshift Tokyo family who steal to get by won the Palme d’Or at Cannes.
Members of this Japanese warrior class served feudal lords, and their code of conduct was later called bushido.
Begun in sections as early as the 5th century BCE, this artificial waterway links Beijing and Hangzhou.
Established by Minamoto no Yoritomo in the late 12th century, this first Japanese shogunate was named for its seaside headquarters town.
This short-lived Chinese ruling house reunified the country in 589 and was succeeded by the Tang in 618.
According to legend, Dangun founded this first Korean kingdom in 2333 BCE.
In 2018, this South Korean county hosted the Winter Olympics.
This Japanese era name began on May 1, 2019, when Emperor Naruhito took the throne.
In 1970, this Japanese city hosted Expo ’70, the first world’s fair held in Asia.
Opened in 2018, this roughly 55-kilometer bridge-and-tunnel crossing spans the Pearl River estuary to link three cities.
clues.a: What is the Hong Kong–Zhuhai–Macao Bridge?

clues.q: In 2003, this astronaut became the first person China sent into space, aboard Shenzhou 5.
This blue robotic cat from the 22nd century pulls futuristic gadgets out of his four-dimensional pocket.
Akira Toriyama’s manga follows Son Goku and friends on quests for seven magical wish-granting orbs.
In Hajime Isayama’s manga, Eren Yeager and the rest of humanity hide behind enormous walls from giant man-eaters.
Which manga artist, nicknamed the “God of Manga,” created Astro Boy?
This Japanese term names manga aimed at young girls, the category that includes “Sailor Moon.”
Native to the mountains of central China, especially Sichuan, this black-and-white bear eats mostly bamboo.
Folding a thousand origami versions of this long-legged bird, a symbol of longevity, is said to grant a wish.
This two-humped camel, named for an ancient Central Asian region, is native to the Gobi.
At Jigokudani in Nagano, these red-faced primates famously soak in hot springs during snowy winters.
Called takhi in Mongolia, this endangered wild horse was reintroduced there in the 1990s and is named for a Russian explorer.

questions.q: Korean dish of thin marinated grilled beef?
Traditional Japanese robe tied with an obi?
Board game called weiqi in Chinese and baduk in Korean?
Japanese word for a hot spring?
In Chinese philosophy, the partner of yin?
Japanese dish of battered, deep-fried seafood and vegetables?
Chinese practice of arranging spaces for harmonious energy?
Japanese island prefecture whose capital is Naha?

clues.q: BTS’s management company, renamed HYBE in 2021, was originally known by this name.
clues.hint: Its old name suggests a chart-topping song.

clues.q: Led by drummer-pianist Yoshiki and singer Toshi, this Japanese band pioneered the flamboyant “visual kei” rock style.
clues.hint: A single letter plus a country’s name.

clues.q: One of Cantopop’s “Four Heavenly Kings,” this singer is often hailed as the “God of Songs.”
clues.hint: His 1993 Mandarin album “The Goodbye Kiss” sold millions.

clues.q: Born in Shenyang in 1982, this classical pianist performed at the opening ceremony of the 2008 Beijing Olympics.
clues.hint: His given name repeats his surname.

clues.q: Brought from the Asian mainland more than a thousand years ago, this is the ancient court music of Japan’s imperial household.
clues.hint: Its name means “elegant music.”

clues.q: In this 1997 Miyazaki film, the young prince Ashitaka is caught between an ironworks town and ancient forest gods.
clues.hint: Its heroine, San, was raised by wolves.

clues.q: This 2002 Hong Kong police thriller starring Andy Lau and Tony Leung was remade by Martin Scorsese as “The Departed.”
clues.hint: Both leads are undercover moles.

clues.q: Bong Joon-ho’s 2013 English-language film is set aboard a train that endlessly circles a frozen Earth.
clues.hint: Based on a French graphic novel.

clues.q: Park Chan-wook’s 2016 film set in 1930s Korea follows a pickpocket hired as a maid to an heiress.
clues.hint: Adapted from Sarah Waters’s novel “Fingersmith.”

clues.q: This Taiwanese director won Best Director at Cannes in 2000 for “Yi Yi,” a portrait of a Taipei family.
clues.hint: He also directed “A Brighter Summer Day.”

clues.q: Ruling China from 960 to 1279, this imperial house saw movable type invented and paper money widely used.
clues.hint: Its capitals were Kaifeng and later Hangzhou.

clues.q: This 15th-century Joseon king commissioned the Korean alphabet and is honored with the title “the Great.”
clues.hint: He appears on South Korea’s 10,000-won note.

clues.q: Chinese chronicles of the 3rd century describe this shaman queen who ruled the Japanese land of Yamatai.
clues.hint: She sent envoys to the Chinese kingdom of Wei.

clues.q: This Ming admiral led seven great “treasure fleet” voyages across the Indian Ocean between 1405 and 1433.
clues.hint: He was a Muslim court eunuch from Yunnan.

clues.q: This 7th-century Buddhist monk traveled from Tang China to India, and his journey inspired a famous classic novel.
clues.hint: He brought hundreds of scriptures back to Chang’an.

clues.q: In 1983, this Kyoto company released the Family Computer, or Famicom, in Japan.
clues.hint: It began as a playing-card maker.

clues.q: Founded in 1938 as a small trading company in Daegu, this firm grew into South Korea’s largest business group.
clues.hint: Its name means “three stars.”

clues.q: In which year did Nagano, Japan, host the Winter Olympics?
In 2012, this novelist, whose “Red Sorghum” became Zhang Yimou’s first film, won the Nobel Prize in Literature.
clues.hint: His pen name means “don’t speak.”

clues.q: Opened in 1994, this Osaka-area airport was built on an artificial island in the bay.
clues.hint: Its three-letter code is KIX.

clues.q: In Japanese folklore, these clever shape-shifting animals grow extra tails as they age.
clues.hint: Statues of them guard Inari shrines.

clues.q: Born from a stone, this Monkey King wreaked havoc in Heaven before escorting a monk on a pilgrimage.
clues.hint: His magic staff can shrink or grow.

clues.q: This Shinto sun goddess is enshrined at Ise and is the mythical ancestor of Japan’s imperial family.
clues.hint: She once hid in a cave, darkening the world.

clues.q: In the Chinese legend behind the Qixi Festival, a flock of these birds forms a bridge so the weaver girl and cowherd can meet once a year.
clues.hint: Black-and-white members of the crow family.

clues.q: In Chinese mythology, this goddess molded the first humans from yellow clay and patched the broken sky.
clues.hint: Often shown with a serpent’s tail.

clues.q: This Cantonese dining tradition serves small plates like har gow and siu mai alongside pots of tea.
clues.hint: Often wheeled around on carts.

clues.q: This thick, chewy Japanese wheat noodle is often served in a dashi-based broth.
clues.hint: Much thicker than soba.

clues.q: Partly oxidized, this tea style falls between green and black tea and is a specialty of Fujian and Taiwan.
clues.hint: Tieguanyin is a famous variety.

clues.q: This Sichuan dish of bean curd in fiery chili-bean sauce is traditionally said to be named for a pockmarked old woman.
clues.hint: Sichuan peppercorns give it a numbing tingle.

clues.q: This aged, fermented dark tea from Yunnan is named for a historic tea-trading town and is often pressed into cakes.
clues.hint: It can be aged for decades, like wine.

questions.q: Which Chinese dynasty built the Forbidden City in Beijing?
Which South Korean city was the capital of the Silla kingdom?
Which Chinese city is famous for the karst peaks along the Li River?
What is the Korean dish of chewy rice cakes simmered in spicy red sauce?
What is the Japanese art of growing miniature trees in containers?

rounds.name: Final Round
rounds.q: Built around 256 BCE under the Qin governor Li Bing, this UNESCO-listed irrigation system in Sichuan still waters the Chengdu Plain without a dam.
rounds.hint: A “fish mouth” levee splits the Min River.
